reason: The support cells' membrane sheets suggest insulation around the motor neuron fibers, matching the goal.
expectation: The support cells will insulate the outgoing nerve fibers.

effect: The fibers and support cells formed motor nerves, completing the insulation goal; the next goal is to connect sight to muscle commands.
reaction: The segmented wrapping and gaps make the insulation more concrete.
reason: The eyes' sensory nerves lead toward a central connection, so connecting them to the central nervous system seems like a useful first step.
expectation: The visual sensory route will connect the eyes to the central nervous system.

effect: The eyes now send visual information to the brain; the motor route still needs to connect commands to the muscles.
reaction: The distinction between seeing the target and producing force is clear.
reason: Motor nerves appear to be the next link between the seeing control system and muscle commands.
expectation: The motor nerves will connect outgoing commands to the seeing control system.

effect: The motor nerves now carry outgoing routes from the control system, but their endings still need to attach to the muscles.
reaction: The unattached endings make the next connection clear.
reason: The arm framework contains the muscles that the outgoing nerves need to reach.
expectation: The motor nerve endings will connect to the arm muscles.

effect: The guided arm connects visual input to outgoing muscle commands; the remaining goal is to return information about arm position.
reaction: The input and output arrows make the two signal directions clear.
reason: The stretch receptors detect changes in muscle length, which can provide information about the arm's position.
expectation: The receptors will respond to muscle-length changes and produce sensory information.

effect: Muscle-length changes now produce a sensory route toward the central nervous system; it still needs to connect to the guided arm.
reaction: The two poses make the source of position information clear.
reason: The guided arm contains the control system and muscles that the position information needs to reach.
expectation: The sensory route will connect the arm's position information to its control system.

effect: The position information route now connects muscle sensors to the central nervous system, completing the chapter's feedback goal.
reaction: The eyes-closed inset ties the sensory route back to the opening example.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting the position information route to the guided arm was most worthwhile: it brought sensory feedback together with the earlier sight and motor pathways and explained how the arm can be guided without watching it.

leastWorthwhile.text: Adding the motor nerves to the seeing control system felt like an expected intermediate connection. Its picture showed unattached endings, but the action was less revealing than connecting those endings to the arm.

surprise.text: The segmented wrapping, with gaps between the supporting cells, made nerve insulation more specific than I expected.

arbitrary.text: No action felt especially arbitrary. The titles and pictures gave a practical reason for each connection, though the game did not explain in detail how the brain uses the sensory signals.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: connecting sensory information, control and muscle action was clear, and I am curious how other body systems would contribute.
